sources.prompt: Edit this supplied original pixel-art sprite sheet for the same game. Preserve the EXACT character identity and sprite-art style: Mira is the small young adult brown-haired woman with tousled brown bob, a tiny white flower clip on her hair, pink rolled-sleeve blouse, charcoal trousers, brown boots, utility belt. Preserve her body size, outfit, face, hairstyle and black/brown pixel outlines as closely as possible. All character poses face left (party stands at right). Replace EVERY long spear in EVERY original pose with a compact handmade spring-powered mechanical bolt launcher: small brown wooden grip/stock, squat dark iron short barrel pointed left, visible brass coiled spring and bolted plates, decidedly village workshop gadget. No long shaft, no spearhead, no giant weapon. She uses the launcher appropriately in hand at waist/chest level, rests/stows it for kneeling poses. In original attack sequence replace overhead spear windup with cocking the spring, replace spear thrust with two-handed aimed launch/recoil, and recovery with lowering the launcher. In guard use braced launcher held close. Victory a relieved confident smile and small tool raised while launcher rests at hip, defeat kneeling exhausted without any spear. KEEP authentic clean limited-palette SNES pixel art, hard square pixels, no smooth illustration, no outlines around cells. OUTPUT A FULL NEW 4-COLUMN x 5-ROW SHEET with EXACTLY 20 separate cells on transparent background, no text, no cell dividers. The first FOUR rows correspond row-major to all sixteen original poses in their existing order (2 idle; 3 attack; 2 guard; 2 hurt; 2 victory; 2 defeat; 3 walk). Keep entire actor in each cell with broad clear margins and same character scale. Fifth/bottom row: cell17 overclock prep (standing, launcher holstered, holding a tiny mechanical controller at chest, other hand readies a tool); cell18 overclock active command (same character, leaning toward left slightly, turning the controller crank/tool with a purposeful encouraging expression, small amber spark near controller); cell19 overclock recovery (controller lowers, satisfied calm expression, no magic); cell20 the matching standalone compact bolt launcher PROP ONLY horizontal left-facing view, no hand or body. Every one of the 19 character sprites has visible whole feet and whole hair, with no clipping. The launcher prop is isolated. Transparent alpha background is essential.

Create a production video-game sprite animation source atlas. STRICT chunky hand-placed-looking SNES pixel art, limited warm iron/brass/brown palette with strong dark pixel outlines, simple readable clusters and absolutely no smooth painting or shiny modern 3D. Transparent background, exactly 4 COLUMNS x 4 ROWS of 16 distinct isolated complete sprites, no text or dividers. A small sturdy workshop helper bot named RIVET, friendly dependable character without a human face, no human limbs. Low squat riveted dark steel boiler-shaped body, round side bolts/exposed fasteners, small amber indicator lamp on front left (no eyes or mouth), FOUR folding insect-like short hinged legs with flat sturdy feet, one chunky short PISTON ARM at the front left. Simple handmade village workshop mechanics, visibly worn but well maintained, modest brass cylinder, dark iron plated shell, exposed spring and fasteners. Always faces LEFT in clear three-quarter side view with body length around1.6 times body height. Consistent design and scale across all16cells. It will be downsampled to a native32x32pixel sprite so bold simple silhouette with four legs readable, no tiny ornate details. Entire bot and feet fully visible within each cell with large clear transparent gaps. Row1 sprites1-4 IDLE slight mechanical breathing and weightshift of feet (distinct poses); Row2 sprites5-6 DEPLOY from folded compact feet to stable four-legged stance; sprites7-8 ATTACK wind-up arm retract then piston jab extends firmly to LEFT, readable contact punch without a fist shape; Row3 sprite9 ATTACK recovery with arm settling down; sprites10-12 OVERCLOCK with stronger amber lamp and tight quick braced stance, tiny warm steam puff, piston cycling (no large effects); Row4 sprites13-14 VICTORY cheerful mechanical bob with frontlegs lifting a little (still nonhuman); sprites15-16 SUSPEND settle down low and fold legs under body then lamp dims (no broken/damaged/defeated imagery). Include all16different authored poses. Make the bot appealing through its low sturdy movement and warm little indicator, no face. Source pixels should be crisp square pixels at a consistent scale. Transparent alpha background only.
